Bruneau - Grand View Fall 2020 Re-Entry Plan The Bruneau - Grand View School District maintains the goal of a ‘typical’ re-entry into the 2020 school year as students return back to school this fall. Our goal is to have as typical as a re-entry as we’re able to, based on requirements / ‘recommendations’ from District Health (SWDH), Centers for Disease Control (CDC), the Gov.’s Office and our State Board of Education (ISBE). As a result, this DRAFT will continue to be updated throughout the summer as the Gov.’s committees to update provide direction & guidance to Idaho schools. Idaho’s State Board has given local school trustees the power to create their own fall reopening plan. Supt. Cantrell encourages Trustees to consider (and ultimately approve) the following 2020 re-entry plan. In the letter from Gov. Little dated July 9, written to school districts as part of the “Idaho Back to School Framework 2020”, Gov. Little indicates, “I expect all our school building to safely reopen in the fall for in-person instruction.” Gov. Little goes on to state, “…we must prioritize the open tin fo school buildings for in-person instruction…” This sentiment echoes the voices of our BGV patrons who are eager for their students to return to our buildings this fall, for face-to-face instruction from their teachers. To this end, BGV will work to offer as typcal of a re-opening as possible. Risk & Liability BGV Trustees must be aware of the potential risk & liability associated with operating school(s) during the COVID-19 pandemic. In April of 2020, the law offices of Anderson, Julian & Hull (who represent BGV in legal matters) issued a notice to Idaho schools, outlining the potential liability schools face during the COVID-19 pandemic. In the conclusion of this memo, AJH encourages Trustees to consider: “What is negligent in the context of reopening, given this unprecedented pandemic?” It is probable, for instance, that reopening during the pendency of the Stay-Home Order will be found to fall below the standard of care for the duty owed, and to support a finding of negligence considering that, in schools, the Order calls for social distancing of six feet per person to be maintained to the greatest extent possible. It is also at least highly possible that, until the curve of overall total cases is flattened, it may be considered negligent to reopen schools. Similarly, if a particular surrounding area, including a county or counties local to a school district, is experiencing community transmission, it may be considered a breach of duty to open local schools. In all decisions made as to whether, and when, to reopen, a district’s 39678 State Highway 78 • Bruneau, Idaho 83604 Phone: 208-834-2260 • Fax: 208-834-2516 D RA F T D RA F T

or charter’s board will want to be sure to consider, and make clear it has considered, the financial, political, economic, and social effects of the reopening plan.” Additionally, ICRMP (Idaho Counties Risk Management Program) issued a statement in March of 2020, specifying that COVID-19 claims are not covered under and District’s insurance policy stating that, “ICRMP’s property and casualty policy does not have coverage related to virus contamination.” These factors & reality must be considered, as Trustees approve students for re-entry into BGV’s schools in the fall of 2020. Masks Supt. Cantrell ordered cloth, reusable masks for the fall 2020 reentry. The masks are manufactured and designed for non- medical personal use and are said to be 99.997% effective against Coronavirus including COVID-19. These are 2 layer masks, washable & reusable ... tested for up to 50 washes. These masks will be used for busing, daily wear by staff/students and for athletics when required. Busing Students will be encouraged (but not required) to wear masks on the school bus during transportation. Reusable BGV masks will be made available upon entry (pick them up from the clean mask bucket) and encouraged (but not required) during the duration of the ride. Upon exiting the bus, students will toss the mask into the used-mask bucket to be washed and re-used at a later date. BGV bus route capacity varies greatly by route. When available, students will be encouraged to sit one student per seat - this is not feasible on all routes, and will not be a requirement for BGV busing when not feasible. Buses will travel with windows cracked 1/2” - 1” when temperatures are above 50 degrees, to improve air circulation on the bus. In warmer weather, the windows will be down further in order to increase air circulation. 39678 State Highway 78 • Bruneau, Idaho 83604 Phone: 208-834-2260 • Fax: 208-834-2516 D RA F T D RA F T

# Page 3^page=3
Bus drivers will be paid additional time to wipe- down each bus seat, after the morning route and the afternoon route - ensuring a sanitized bus for each route. Classroom(s) Students will not be required to wear masks in the classroom, but may if they choose to do so. Reusable masks will be made available to any student who chooses to wear one. Upon recommendation from SWDH, student desks will not face one another but rather they will face forward or face away from one another. Teachers will not be required to wear masks, but reusable BGV masks will be made available to every BGV staff. Food Service FS Staff will be required to wear both masks & gloves while serving the cooked food (but not during the preparation of the food before it is cooked). Hand Sanitization All BGV schools have hand sanitizers in the hallways and in many (if not most) classrooms for daily use. In the fall of 2020, BGV elementary students will engage in hand-washing classes with their teachers, to ensure proper hand washing techniques are known and understood by students. During the transition to lunch, each BGV elementary student will be required to wash their hands prior to lunch - either in the classroom or in the restroom. 39678 State Highway 78 • Bruneau, Idaho 83604 Phone: 208-834-2260 • Fax: 208-834-2516 D RA F T D RA F T

# Page 4^page=4
Screening Staff and students who indicate symptoms consistent with COVID-19 will be sent home. Students indicating symptoms at school will be quarantined in a smaller room (i.e. infirmary, ISS room, etc) until their parents arrive. The room will be disinfected upon the student leaving. Students and staff indicating symptoms consistent with COVID-19 will not be allowed to remain at school. Bus drivers will be offered touchless thermometers to screen students upon entry to the bus. If a student is found to have a fever, they will return to their family. If a student’s family has already left, the driver will contact the school to have the family pick the student up upon arriving at school - meanwhile, the student will be required (not offered) to wear a mask while on the bus. Visitors Visitors within district will be required to wash hands/use hand sanitizer upon entry (in addition to signing into the building, as already required). Visitors visiting from high-spread communities will be required to wear a mask in addition to washing/sanitizing hands. Parent pick-up Elementary parent pick-up will occur in the parent vehicle pick-up line. All students not riding the bus or walking, will be picked-up via the parent pick-up line at the elementary school(s) - parents will not enter the building to pick-up their children at the end of the school day. Lunch Elementary students will only use one side of the lunch table during meal time, to prevent students from sitting directly across from one another as they eat. This may require elementary schools to feed K-2 then 3-5 students based on seating capacity. Rimrock students will be encouraged to spread out in the lunchroom, and permitted to eat in the hallway to allow for increased distance from one another during lunch. 39678 State Highway 78 • Bruneau, Idaho 83604 Phone: 208-834-2260 • Fax: 208-834-2516 D RA F T

This model, from Georgia’s Path to Recovery for K-12 Schools, indications the options of educational models available to schools throughout the COVID-19 crisis. During times of low/no spread, BGV schools will operate with preventative practices. In times of minimal to moderate spread BGV schools will continue traditional operations with enhanced mitigation measures as necessary. If substantial spread occurs in the towns of Oreana, Grand View and/or Bruneau then it may be return to distance/remote learning during a short term closure to allow for a deep cleaning of the facilities and until substantial spread is no longer present in the towns. SWDH will determine the level of spread in our communities. This plan was developed to offer as typical of a re-opening as possible while encouraging adherence to government-developed recommendations to promote student and staff safety while at school.
